Respect him, beta. Just don't hand him your eyes. Your Manoj uncle learned that at twenty-five.

I'm Zubin, a junior structural engineer, and I have admired Afreen ma'am since my first day at the firm. She's designed half the bridges in our district. So when she said at the review, "The old soil report from 2015 is enough; we don't need a new test," my first instinct was to nod.
But I'd walked that site the week before. The riverbank had shifted after two heavy monsoons.
After the meeting, I knocked on her cabin. "Ma'am, can I ask how we decided the 2015 report still fits?"
She looked up, a little surprised. "The soil there hasn't changed in decades."
"You know that ground better than I do," I said. "But I took photos last week. The bank has moved." I put them on her desk.
She studied them for a long time. Then she picked up the phone and asked for a new test. As I left she said, "Good. Keep doing that, young man."

qa.a: The riverbank had shifted after two heavy monsoons.

qa.a: Zubin's first instinct was to nod, because he admired Afreen ma'am and she had designed half the bridges in the district.

qa.a: He asked privately how the decision was reached, acknowledged that she knew the ground better, and then showed his photos as evidence.

I'm Lakshmi. I sat in on the budget meeting last week when Hemant, one of our analysts, did something I'd never seen anyone do with our director.

The director had said, very confidently, that "digital ads never work for our older customers". Everyone nodded. The director has been here twenty years.

Hemant raised his hand. "Sir, may I ask how we know that?"

The director looked surprised. "Experience."

Hemant nodded. "That makes sense. I only ask because last quarter we ran a small test with older customers. The response was better than print." He handed over a single printed chart. "I may be missing something. I'd really value your thoughts."

The director studied the chart for a long time. "Interesting. Let's run a bigger test."

I don't know what Hemant felt inside. But his voice stayed calm and polite the whole time. He respected the director. He just didn't pretend to agree.
